original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of simple polygons.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Open Problem 32: Characterize visibility graphs of simple polygons.
correct_elements: Your draft already points to the right target: the paper’s general characterization problem for visibility graphs of simple polygons, not a neighboring problem about point sets, segments, reconstruction, or coloring. It also correctly asks for an exact classification rather than merely necessary conditions.
missing_details: The paper’s object is the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon: graph vertices correspond bijectively to polygon vertices.
Adjacency must be stated explicitly: two polygon vertices are adjacent iff the straight-line segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon.
Under the paper’s visibility convention, the segment is allowed to pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge.
The question is about which finite simple undirected graphs arise, up to graph isomorphism.
To be fully stand-alone, the formulation should say 'give necessary and sufficient conditions' rather than rely on the informal word 'characterize'.

The scope should stay with simple polygons in the polygon-visibility sense, and not drift to the separate recognition problems in Section 4.1, including the variant where a Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the boundary is supplied.
No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier conventions are involved here; the hidden assumptions are purely geometric/combinatorial.
refined_question: Give necessary and sufficient conditions for a finite simple graph G to be isomorphic to the vertex visibility graph of some simple polygon P in the plane; that is, characterize exactly those graphs for which the vertices of G can be put in bijection with the vertices of P so that two vertices are adjacent in G if and only if the straight-line segment joining the corresponding polygon vertices lies entirely within P, with visibility interpreted as in the paper (segments may pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge).
justification: The draft matches the paper’s official target almost verbatim: Section 4.2 defines the polygon visibility-graph characterization problem and then states Open Problem 32 as 'Characterize visibility graphs of simple polygons.' To make that statement stand alone, one must import the definition of a polygon’s vertex visibility graph from Section 1. Section 4.1 treats recognition as a distinct neighboring problem—both without extra data (Open Problem 28) and with a boundary Hamiltonian cycle provided (Open Problem 30)—so the refined question should not add algorithmic input assumptions or boundary-cycle data that are not part of Open Problem 32. The surrounding discussion in Section 4.2 also confirms that the paper is asking for the general simple-polygon case, after listing characterizations known only for special subclasses such as spiral polygons, towers, and staircase polygons.
